title: A Smarter Approach to Capital Management in Insurance
gist: BCG argues that with European insurers' solvency ratios uniformly strong and the Solvency II Review (early 2027) likely to raise headroom further, investors now value insurers on how reliably capital converts into deployable cash, returns, and growth. Leaders combine an embedded steering framework, AI-enabled forward-looking analytics, and 100+ combined optimization levers (e.g., SAA and asset-intensive reinsurance), yielding results like €4 billion upstreamed and 30bp+ risk-adjusted return gains.

insights.claim: With solvency ratios uniformly strong across major European insurers, investors and analysts now judge insurers on how reliably capital converts into holding-company cash, returns, and growth rather than on headline solvency.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Valuation dispersion among European insurers should increasingly track demonstrated cash conversion, not solvency ratio levels.
insights.quote: Solvency is not the issue for any of these names. The question is what the capital is actually worth.
insights.locator: Sound Capital Management Builds Confidence

insights.claim: Insurers that cannot clearly show how capital turns into cash, returns, and growth can see valuations suffer even when headline solvency ratios and capital generation look strong.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Screen insurers for transparency on capital-to-cash conversion; opaque names with strong solvency may carry a hidden valuation discount.
insights.quote: when an insurer cannot, questions mount and valuations can suffer—even when the headline solvency ratio and capital generation look strong
insights.locator: These questions were not entirely absent

insights.claim: Investor questioning of European insurers now centres on whether reported capital generation is flattered by one-off effects or favorable markets, how it converts to holding-company cash, and why the chosen split among dividends, buybacks, organic growth, and M&A is optimal.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Use these three questions as a diligence checklist when assessing insurer capital-return stories.
insights.quote: How stable and sustainable is reported capital generation, or is it flattered by one-off effects and favorable markets?
insights.locator: For example: How stable and sustainable

insights.claim: UK and Dutch insurers have steered and reported on capital generation and cash remittance for years, while many other European insurers still report capital mainly in solvency terms and treat cash, returns, and growth separately.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: UK and Dutch insurers may have a disclosure-maturity edge; laggard markets could re-rate if they adopt cash-remittance reporting.
insights.locator: Some insurers, particularly those in the UK and the Netherlands

themes.theme: Solvency II Review and deployable capital

insights.claim: The Solvency II Review, taking effect in early 2027, is likely to lift solvency coverage ratios for many European insurers and opens a window for CFOs to reassess capital allocation.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Watch for capital-allocation resets, buyback or M&A announcements around the early-2027 Solvency II changes.
insights.locator: Two developments may raise the bar even higher

insights.claim: Additional regulatory headroom from the Solvency II Review will not automatically become deployable capital, because local statutory and accounting constraints, fungibility, and management buffers determine how much can actually be redeployed, with impact varying by business mix, asset allocation, and balance sheet.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Do not extrapolate higher post-2027 solvency ratios directly into higher distributions; check entity-level fungibility.
insights.quote: one euro of additional regulatory headroom is not necessarily one euro available for redeployment
insights.locator: Two developments may raise the bar even higher

insights.claim: Higher interest rates have supported insurer solvency coverage ratios but left unrealized losses on many local balance sheets, which can constrain conversion of reported capital strength into distributable cash.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Insurers with large local unrealized losses may disappoint on cash remittance despite strong group solvency.
insights.locator: At the same time, higher interest rates

insights.claim: BCG frames insurer capital-management maturity as a progression from regulatory compliance, to managing capital, to integrating KPIs, to optimizing value, built on three elements: steering framework, analytical capabilities, and optimization levers.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Use the maturity ladder to place insurers relative to peers and gauge upside from catching up.
insights.locator: What Best in Class Looks Like

insights.claim: Exchange-listed insurers typically steer by shareholder value measures while mutual insurers lean toward policyholder value, resilience, and long-term surplus, because capital KPIs follow each company's purpose and strategy.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Compare listed versus mutual capital KPIs carefully; metric choice reflects ownership model, not just performance.
insights.locator: At the start of the framework

insights.claim: Leading insurers pre-agree tradeoffs such as growth versus capital return and cash versus capital generation, cascade the logic down to business units, legal entities, and business lines, and hardwire it into budgeting and incentives, turning capital management from reporting into steering.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Management incentive structures tied to capital and cash KPIs are a signal of a best-in-class steering discipline.
insights.quote: turns capital management from a reporting exercise into a steering discipline
insights.locator: Leading insurers deeply embed this steering framework

insights.claim: Leading insurers regularly challenge whether their solvency targets and management buffers remain economically justified, implying excess buffers are a source of releasable capital.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Insurers with conservative buffers versus peers may have latent capital-return capacity.
insights.locator: Leading insurers then hardwire these choices

insights.claim: Many insurers do not know how their business plan will affect capital until after it is underway and cannot drill into business lines, risk types, or drivers, which leaves value on the table.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Insurers investing in capital analytics should show fewer negative capital surprises versus plan.
insights.quote: Many insurers don’t know how their business plan will impact capital until after the plan is set in motion.
insights.locator: Analytical Capabilities.

insights.claim: Leading insurers use near-real-time KPI monitoring, AI-supported root-cause dashboards, and what-if scenario analysis that produces answers in minutes rather than weeks, with AI as the key enabler of forward-looking capital analysis.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Demand signal for AI-driven actuarial, capital-modeling, and finance analytics tooling among insurers.
insights.quote: AI is the key enabler of this shift
insights.locator: Leading insurers are investing significantly in analytics

insights.claim: BCG identifies well over a hundred capital-optimization levers across product and business mix, assets and ALM, reinsurance, models and assumptions, legal-entity capital and fungibility, treasury and capital structure, and portfolio actions, and leaders apply several simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Insurers pulling multiple levers at once are likelier to deliver outsized capital releases.
insights.locator: We have identified well over a hundred distinct levers

insights.claim: A global top-ten insurer identified and upstreamed €4 billion of capital from business units, and a medium-sized European monoliner increased bottom-line capital generation by €300 million per year, by using multiple optimization levers.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Sizes the prize: coordinated capital optimization can fund multi-billion buybacks or M&A at large insurers.
insights.quote: a global top-ten insurer identified and upstreamed €4 billion of capital from business units
insights.locator: We have identified well over a hundred distinct levers

insights.claim: Optimization levers interact: internal reinsurance can free local capital for growth or riskier asset allocation, moving off overly conservative reserves or models can raise solvency for reinvestment, and a larger market-risk budget lifts returns while consuming solvency headroom.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Assess insurer capital actions as a combined package; one lever's release often funds another's risk-taking.
insights.locator: The second dimension is breadth

themes.theme: Asset allocation and reinsurance as capital tools

insights.claim: The typical insurer strategic asset allocation process optimizes against risk appetite using proxy metrics and tests only a handful of candidate portfolios in capital models, leaving significant profit potential on the table.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Insurers still using proxy-based SAA have untapped investment-return upside.
insights.quote: The outcome is an SAA that leaves significant profit potential on the table.
insights.locator: Strategic Asset Allocation.

insights.claim: By genuinely linking capital, actuarial, and asset models for real-time sensitivity analysis, BCG has seen European insurers lift risk-adjusted investment returns by 30 basis points or more, worth tens or even hundreds of millions of euros in additional annual earnings depending on balance sheet size.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: A 30bp risk-adjusted yield uplift is material for large balance-sheet insurers' earnings guidance.
insights.quote: lifted risk-adjusted investment returns by 30 basis points or more
insights.locator: The experience in the ALM or investment committee

insights.claim: Reinsurance has shifted from mainly proportional risk transfer to a deliberate capital instrument; in life and health, asset-intensive and ALM reinsurance can transfer long-duration liabilities with selected interest rate, credit spread, currency, inflation, or biometric risks while assets often stay with the cedent.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Supports continued growth in asset-intensive and ALM reinsurance demand from life insurers; relevant for reinsurers and capital-structure investors.
insights.quote: has become a deliberate capital instrument that releases solvency and reserve capital, transfers asset and market risk, and steers cash and earnings across the group
insights.locator: Internal and External Reinsurance.

insights.claim: Insurers that can convert capital strength into cash, growth, and distributions and show how will be rewarded, while those that cannot will face valuation pressure, making capital management a strategic rather than technical priority.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Expect re-rating divergence between insurers with credible capital-to-cash equity stories and those without.
insights.quote: Insurers that can convert capital strength into cash, growth, and distributions—and can show how—will be rewarded
insights.locator: A Strategic Agenda for CFOs

insights.claim: CFOs should ask five questions: how they compare to peers on capital generation, cash conversion, capital productivity, and distributions; how much capital is truly deployable; where capital creates most value; whether full optimization potential is used; and where the next euro of capital should go.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Mirror these five questions in investor engagement with insurer management.
insights.locator: Here are five questions CFOs should ask

insights.claim: Benefits of capital management take time to materialize because assessing opportunities, prioritizing, and implementing solutions follow building the capability, so insurers that delay will lag.
insights.speaker: Anastasios Panagiotou
insights.so_what: Capital-optimization programs announced now likely pay off over multi-year horizons; set expectations accordingly.
insights.locator: The progression of capital management
